title: Muthoot FinCorp Bags BCCI Title Sponsorship for Indian Cricket Until 2028
excerpt: The Kerala-based lender replaces IDFC First Bank for two home seasons, covering about 35 internationals and major domestic tournaments at a reported Rs 4.3 crore per match.
body:
• Muthoot FinCorp has acquired BCCI title sponsorship rights for India's home cricket until March 31, 2028, covering about 35 home internationals.
  • Reports put the deal at up to Rs 4.3 crore per match and up to Rs 150 crore in total, below the BCCI's Rs 4.85 crore per-match base price but above IDFC First Bank's Rs 4.2 crore rate.
  • The rights cover senior men's and women's teams, India A and Under-19 sides, and domestic tournaments including the Ranji Trophy.
  • The partnership began with India's ODI series against the West Indies starting September 27 in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, Muthoot's home state.

Muthoot FinCorp has acquired the title sponsorship rights for Indian cricket for the next two home seasons, in a deal that runs until March 31, 2028. According to SportsMint Media, the Kerala-based non-banking financial company replaces IDFC First Bank and will cover around 35 home internationals, reported as 10 Tests, 12 ODIs and 13 T20Is.

The sponsorship, referred to in reports as 'Blue Muthoot', was negotiated after the Board of Control for Cricket in India received no bids by its August 13 Invitation to Tender deadline. Coverage on IPL.com, citing Cricbuzz, said industry sources attributed the lack of interest in part to the high base price, and that the BCCI then held direct discussions with interested companies.

What the deal is worth

SportsMint reported Muthoot FinCorp is set to pay up to Rs 4.3 crore per match, in a package reported at up to Rs 150 crore. That figure is marginally higher than the Rs 4.2 crore per match paid by IDFC First Bank, whose agreement ended in August, but below the BCCI's base price of Rs 4.85 crore per match for this cycle. A separate account on SportsAdda noted the board's own statement gave no fee, and that reported totals ranged between about Rs 150 crore and Rs 170 crore depending on the per-match rate used.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IMDDcCBdyzU

IDFC First Bank's previous deal, signed in 2023, covered 56 matches and was valued at about Rs 235.2 crore, according to the reports. The new cycle is shorter in match count but carries a slightly higher per-match rate, even after a tender that drew no takers.

"Muthoot FinCorp's association as Title Sponsor reflects the strength and reach of Indian cricket and the connection it has with people across the country."

— Mithun Manhas, BCCI President

What the rights cover

The agreement goes well beyond the senior men's team. According to SportsMint, it includes India's senior men's and women's national teams, India A men's and women's teams, India B men's team, Under-19 men's and women's teams, and other designated teams. It also covers domestic competitions including the Ranji Trophy, Irani Cup, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy, Deodhar Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.

BCCI Honorary Secretary Devajit Saikia said the association extending across senior, A-team, age-group and domestic cricket was particularly encouraging, while Joint Managing Director Thomas George Muthoot said cricket provided a meaningful way for the company to connect with the Indian public.

A tender that found no bidders

The path to this deal underlines a softer sponsorship market than the BCCI expected. With no bids submitted by August 13, the board approached prospective partners directly. Reports named Google Gemini, IDFC First Bank, Spinny and SBI Life among those approached. SBI Life ultimately signed as an associate partner, alongside Campa and ChatGPT, for two seasons through March 2028.

For Muthoot FinCorp, previously associated with Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL, the title deal gives exposure across broadcast, digital and stadium platforms for virtually every match played in India over the next two seasons.

What happens next

The partnership took effect immediately, starting with India's three-match ODI series against the West Indies from September 27 in Thiruvananthapuram. For diaspora fans following India's home season from abroad, the 'Blue Muthoot' branding will be the title attached to series coverage, venues and domestic tournaments through March 2028.
